clue.text: Following not so quiet penguins perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the remaining letters may be some other arrangement, signalling an anagram
not so quiet says the penguins lose their quiet letter, a removal

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Penguins trailing behind someone, a little noisier than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so quiet' removes P from PENGUINS, leaving ENGUINS; 'perhaps' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ensuing comes next in sequence, as a result or successor does.

clue.text: Ended game after ties .- roughly assessed

indicators.note: after puts the game piece behind the rearranged letters
roughly means not precisely, so the letters of ties are loosely rearranged

parts.note: a chess game ended by checkmate is mated

explanation.surface: A game finishes after several draws, and is judged loosely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks part of the definition 'roughly assessed', but it is the anagram signal turning TIES into ESTI.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge an amount approximately.

indicators.note: get here means the ship receives something inside it, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: aboard means on a ship, abbreviated SS (steamship)
print is a patterned cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Rushing to load cloth onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' is the old shorthand for being on a steamship; 'get' says the ship takes the cloth inside, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprints are short fast runs, as dashes are.

definitions.meaning: in music, the gap between two notes
breaks in the middle of a theatre performance

explanation.surface: A football pitch where play keeps being halted.
explanation.definitionFit: Musically the gap between notes is a named step such as a fifth; theatrically the breaks halfway through a show.

indicators.note: included means the letters sit inside the words stringy beans

explanation.surface: A cook complains about stringy beans in the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To gybe is to swing a sail across when sailing downwind, altering direction.

definitions.meaning: a small dish served first in a meal
at a race meeting, the official who sets the runners off, or a horse that runs

explanation.surface: Someone snacking on canapes at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A first course opens a meal, and at a race meeting an official begins each race while each runner is a participant.

parts.note: alludes to the proverbial wolf in lamb's clothing, the disguise a cunning predator wears

explanation.surface: A football club's cunning new kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is also the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, adding a surface about team strips.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguised predator wears the woolly hide of a ewe, the proverbial cover for hidden menace.

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A tax, naturally enough.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: About to enter neat oriental galley

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the next

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy
re means about or concerning
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: Something tidy and Eastern is about to go into a ship's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galley' looks like a ship's kitchen but here is the oared warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient warship rowed by three banks of oars, a type of oared ship.

parts.note: rig is equipment or gear
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls their equipment being stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means inflexible, unable to bend.

clue.text: Game we take back to desert

indicators.note: take back tells us to read the two pieces backwards as one run

parts.note: taken as written
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to go back to the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we' is padding for the surface; 'take back' turns the whole run round. Tarot is also a card game played in parts of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot (tarock) is a family of trick-taking card games as well as a fortune-telling pack.

clue.text: Bring about every method of making an opening

indicators.note: about means the word bring is placed around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
every and each both mean all taken singly

explanation.surface: A guide to the ways of opening something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'method of' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition; 'about' is the container signal, not a vague 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaching a wall or defence is breaking a gap through it.

clue.text: Number halved by association of these workers

definitions.text: Number halved by association of these workers

parts.words: Number halved by association of these workers
parts.note: the first half of the word Number gives the initials of the National Union of Mineworkers, the trade association of the workers wanted

explanation.surface: A trade union cuts its membership by half.
explanation.walkthrough: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British coal workers' union famous for the 1984-85 strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal workers who belong to the NUM dig underground for a living.

clue.text: Date ship was wrecked in the strait

indicators.note: was wrecked signals that the letters of the two words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Records note the day a vessel went down in a narrow channel.
explanation.walkthrough: SPITHEAD is the stretch of water off Portsmouth, England, a famous naval anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spithead is the channel between Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight, a sea passage.

parts.note: in As You Like It Rosalind says men are April when they woo; such suitors are taken in, like those tricked on the first of the month

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's heroine calls her suitors fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosalind says 'men are April when they woo, December when they wed'. 'Dupes' points to victims of pranks on 1 April.
explanation.definitionFit: Victims of pranks played on the first of April are tricked people, dupes.

indicators.note: returns means the word for something valuable is read backwards

parts.note: an asset is a useful or valuable thing

explanation.surface: A woman gives back a treasured possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a woman's name, so it stands for a female pronoun.

parts.note: reads as a porcelain ornament, but means a breed of dog that originated in China, named after its old capital

explanation.surface: A porcelain figurine of a dog on the mantelpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a small long-haired toy dog first kept by the Chinese imperial court in Peking.

clue.text: Wrongly put Ezra amongst Anne's early Christians

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are set in a wrong order, an anagram

parts.note: Anne's gives its letters with the S kept

explanation.surface: Ezra misplaced among Anne's religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... amongst' is surface glue: the letters of EZRA and ANNES are simply mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazarenes was an early name for followers of Jesus of Nazareth.

clue.text: Unnatural vice, consuming spirit, according to the Gospel

indicators.note: consuming means the jumbled letters swallow the next piece
unnatural signals the letters of vice in an unnatural order

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly spirit

explanation.surface: A preacher condemns perverted sin and drink in gospel terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnatural' rearranges the vice letters to EVIC, which 'consuming' wraps round the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic describes what accords with the teachings of the four Gospels.

parts.note: a digest is a summary or synopsis

indicators.note: returned means the letters for number one are read backwards

parts.note: first is number one, written No. I

explanation.surface: A summary sent back first so it can be absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives NO I (No. 1, number one); 'returned' turns that into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Digestion is how the body absorbs food, assimilating it into tissue.

clue.text: Man of taste, our Monsieur? Get out!

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with refined palate is shown the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of good food and drink.

clue.text: Zoology originally involved bear and this animal

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word zoology
involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters of bear are mixed up

explanation.surface: A zoology lesson mixing up a bear and another creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra is a striped African animal of the horse family.

clue.text: Ancient inhabitant holds ten in prison

indicators.note: holds means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a Briton was an inhabitant of ancient Britain
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A primitive local keeps ten people locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIXTON is a prison in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Brixton is a London jail, HMP Brixton.

definitions.meaning: Reynard the fox loses his tail, called a brush, at the end of a hunt

explanation.surface: A snub followed by the sad end of a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: Reynard is the traditional name for a fox; in British fox hunting the tail is the brush, cut off as a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt dismissal is a snub; and a fox losing its tail literally has its tail cut off.

clue.text: Fundamental to put graduates in charge

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: Essential to give graduates responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means essential, at the root of something.

clue.text: A great beast in place of St Augustine

definitions.meaning: a large African river animal, short for hippopotamus
the North African town where Augustine was bishop

explanation.surface: A huge creature lives in the saint's town.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustine was bishop of Hippo Regius, in present-day Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name of the river horse, and the Roman city where Augustine served as bishop.

explanation.surface: Someone irritating who nevertheless means well.
explanation.definitionFit: A wearying person tests patience, and someone making every effort is having a go.

definitions.meaning: a structural timber in a building

explanation.surface: Ray serves as an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light shines out, and a horizontal timber supports a building's roof.

indicators.note: scrambled tells us the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Instructions to signal NATO headquarters, with Rome's message garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE was NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal with flags held at arm positions is to communicate across a distance by flag code.

parts.note: Nat is a man's name, short for Nathaniel
Al is a man's name, short for Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: A pair of men of noble birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is an adjective relating to the time or place a person is born.

definitions.note: fruit can be plural, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Is that corn, or is it some other fruit?
explanation.definitionFit: Citrons are large lemon-like citrus fruits grown for their thick peel.

clue.text: Two of a family one caught in such a lodge

definitions.note: adjectival sense: describing a lodge of this kind

parts.note: ma is a mother, one member of a family
a son is another member of a family
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A mother and son both caught up in a secretive fraternal society.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as the kind of lodge, i.e. a Freemasons' lodge, so the answer is used adjectivally.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemasons' meeting place is called a lodge, and the adjective describes things of the Freemasons.
